answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a raven as the anchor of the cost.
